hypothesis: Matchday's independent model, built on opponent-adjusted efficiency and four-factors profiles derived from CollegeBasketballData box scores, holds information about men's college basketball fixtures that the closing sportsbook consensus has not yet priced at lock time.
target: Beat the closing no-vig consensus on NCAAM fixtures. This is a forecasting claim only. Matchday places no wagers, so the target is accuracy against the closing line, not profit after margin.
primary_metric: Mean closing-minus-lock probability movement toward Matchday's selected outcome (closing line value), with a 95% deterministic game-date block bootstrap interval. The claim is upheld only if the interval lies entirely above zero.
secondary_metric: Paired log loss of Matchday's independent probabilities against the closing no-vig consensus over the same fixtures, reported with the same interval method. Reported always; it cannot rescue a failed primary metric.
decision_rule: Evaluate once, after the final graded fixture of the 2026-27 regular season, and only if every minimum is met. Upheld if the primary metric's 95% interval lies entirely above zero. Not upheld in every other case, including an interval containing zero. No subset, sport, date range, metric, or threshold may be chosen after collection begins; a segment analysis may be published only as exploratory and may never restate the outcome. A failed result is recorded as a failed result.
notes: Registered before the 2026-27 season begins and before the NCAAM model exists. The model artifact must be built and frozen before artifact_freeze_deadline; if that deadline passes with no frozen cohort, this declaration is void and no claim may be made from the season's evidence.

NCAAM was chosen over MLB deliberately. MLB's dominant variable is the starting pitcher, which the market prices and Matchday has no licensed source for (PROVIDER_COMPLIANCE.md), so the MLB gap is an information asymmetry rather than a modelling deficit. NCAAM has an approved data source already wired, genuine differentiated talent data, and roughly 360 Division I programmes that sportsbooks cannot all price sharply.

Closing line value is the primary metric because match outcomes are too noisy to settle this question in a reasonable sample; line movement carries far less variance and answers in hundreds of fixtures rather than thousands.
The lock lead floor exists so the claim cannot be won by locking late. A pick recorded moments before tip-off has nothing to be right early about.
